title: Minimal parabolic flag projections and rank-one coordinates
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]: smooth, connected, affine and of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, such that every surjective homomorphism from a semisimple group with finite central kernel is an isomorphism. Solvable means that successive scheme-theoretic commutator subgroups become trivial; central means commuting after every scalar extension. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq B\subseteq G$, where $B$ is a Borel subgroup, and take $Q=G/B$, roots $\Phi$, positive roots $\Phi^+$ and simple roots $\Delta$ from [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Fix $\alpha\in\Delta$, let $U_{\pm\alpha}$ be the root subgroups of [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations], and let $s_\alpha\in N_G(T)(F)/T(F)$ be the reflection of [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections]. Choose a representative $n_s\in N_G(T)(F)$ and a root coordinate $u_\alpha:\mathbf G_a\xrightarrow{\sim}U_\alpha$. Let $P_\alpha$ be the closed subgroup generated by $B$ and $U_{-\alpha}$, and take the represented fppf quotient $H_\alpha=G/P_\alpha$ and its Zariski locally trivial right $P_\alpha$-torsor $G\to H_\alpha$ from [lem-sfb-standard-parabolic-levi-charts] for $I=\{\alpha\}$. Here fppf means faithfully flat covers locally of finite presentation. One has $n_s\in P_\alpha(F)$ and
$$P_\alpha(K)=B(K)\sqcup B(K)n_sB(K)$$
for every algebraically closed extension $K/F$. The natural map
$$q_\alpha:Q\longrightarrow H_\alpha,\qquad gB\longmapsto gP_\alpha$$
is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], projective [def-pc-projective-morphism], and Zariski locally trivial with fibre $P_\alpha/B\simeq\mathbf P^1_F$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Its fibre over $P_\alpha$ is the closed subscheme $P_\alpha/B\subseteq Q$. The quotient map $P_\alpha\to P_\alpha/B$ is a Zariski locally trivial right $B$-torsor. In $P_\alpha/B$ the complement of the point $B$ is the open affine line
$$a\longmapsto u_\alpha(a)n_sB,$$
and multiplication $(a,b)\mapsto u_\alpha(a)n_sb$ is an isomorphism $\mathbf A^1_F\times_F B\xrightarrow{\sim}Bn_sB$ onto its inverse image in $P_\alpha$. On this affine coordinate the left $T$-action is $a\mapsto\alpha(t)a$, as an identity over every commutative $F$-algebra. All assertions hold in every characteristic.

source.place: Section 2.1, printed pp.62--63: P_i=B union Bs_iB, Schubert curves P_i/B, and the paragraph on the locally trivial principal P-bundle and projection f_P; Section 2.2.1 diagram (D), printed pp.66--67. Scheme-theoretic torsor formulation and relative projectivity made explicit. Author-hosted PDF read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Put $P=P_\alpha$, $L=C_G(T_\alpha)$, $D=B\cap L$ and $R=R_u(P)$. Apply the standard-parabolic lemma with $I=\{\alpha\}$: it gives $P=R\rtimes L$, $B=R\rtimes D$, with $D$ a Borel of $L$ containing $T$. The rank-one-reflection lemma identifies this same centralizer $L$ as reductive of semisimple rank one. Thus its rank-one classification applies. These are subgroup-scheme decompositions, so they can be used over arbitrary $F$-algebras, including nonreduced ones.

Choose the isomorphism of pairs $(L,T)$ given by the split-rank-one classification. It identifies them with a split torus factor times $J$, with diagonal maximal torus, where $J$ is $\operatorname{SL}_2$, $\operatorname{GL}_2$, or $\operatorname{PGL}_2$. We may interchange the two matrix axes so that $\alpha$ is the upper-root character. To identify $D$ scheme-theoretically, write $D=P(\lambda)$ using the regular-cocharacter Borel lemma. Its Lie-algebra formula and the positive root $\alpha$ of $D$ give $\langle\alpha,\lambda\rangle>0$. Conjugation multiplies the upper matrix entry by a positive power of the parameter and the lower entry by its negative power. The limit exists exactly when the lower entry is zero; this is a coefficient identity over any algebra. The central torus factor acts trivially. Consequently $D$ is the torus factor times the upper-triangular subgroup $D_J$ of $J$. For $\operatorname{PGL}_2$ this calculation is checked after fppf lifting to invertible matrices and descends, since scalar matrices preserve both the limit condition and upper triangularity.

source.place: 20.33--20.34, pp.418--419 (rank-one hypothesis and corrected derived groups as in the cited DAG lemma); 21.32--21.35, pp.434--435

proof.text:
Here is the quotient calculation in these matrix models. Send a matrix $M$ to its first-column line $[M_{11}:M_{21}]$. On the two standard affine charts of $\mathbf P^1$, regular lifts are
$$S_0(z)=I_2+zE_{21},\qquad S_1(a)=aE_{11}-E_{12}+E_{21}.$$
Here $E_{ij}$ is the $2\times2$ matrix unit and $I_2$ is the identity matrix. Both have determinant one and first-column lines $[1:z]$ and $[a:1]$. On either chart every matrix over it factors uniquely as $S_iD_J$: its second factor is $S_i^{-1}M$, which is upper triangular because its first column spans the first coordinate line. This gives inverse regular maps between the inverse image of the chart and the chart times $D_J$. For $\operatorname{PGL}_2$, the same formula on matrix lifts is independent of their scalar ambiguity; it therefore holds as an identity of fppf sheaves. The unused split torus factor is contained in $D$ and cancels from right cosets. These explicit sections and factorizations identify the represented right-coset sheaf $L/D$ with $\mathbf P^1_F$, with a Zariski locally trivial right $D$-torsor $L\to L/D$. The identity coset is $[1:0]$ and its complement is the chart $[a:1]$.

source.place: 20.33--20.34, pp.418--419; explicit two-by-two matrix calculation of the homogeneous quotient

proof.text: The semidirect-product formulas give an isomorphism of fppf coset sheaves $P/B\simeq L/D$: send the class of $(r,l)$ to $lD$, with inverse induced by $L\hookrightarrow P$. Indeed $R\subseteq B$ and $r l=l(l^{-1}rl)$, so $(r,l)B=lB$; and two $L$-points differ by $B$ precisely when they differ by $D=B\cap L$. These formulas hold locally for the fppf topology and hence on the quotient sheaves. In particular $P/B$ is represented by the projective line just constructed. The sections $S_i$ lifted to $P$ trivialize $P\to P/B$: for a lift $s_i$ the mutually inverse maps are $(x,b)\mapsto s_i(x)b$ and $p\mapsto(\bar p,s_i(\bar p)^{-1}p)$. This proves the right $B$-torsor assertion with actual Zariski sections.

source.place: 21.91, pp.453--454, followed by the explicit coset and section formulas

proof.text: In the matrix model let $w=E_{21}-E_{12}$. It normalizes the diagonal torus and exchanges the two root spaces, so its class in $N_L(T)/T$ is the unique nonidentity class of the rank-one-reflection lemma. Its image $n_0$ therefore represents $s_\alpha$ in $N_G(T)/T$. The chosen representative is $n_s=n_0t_0$ for some $t_0\in T(F)$; hence $n_s\in L(F)\subseteq P(F)$ and $n_sB=n_0B$. The upper-root subgroup of $L$ is the matrix upper-unitriangular subgroup: in the matrix models this is a smooth connected $T$-normalized subgroup with the prescribed root tangent space, so the uniqueness assertion of the root-subgroup lemma identifies it with $U_\alpha$. The chosen group coordinate $u_\alpha$ thus has matrix coordinate $x\mapsto cx$, $c\in F^\times$. Indeed an automorphism of $\mathbf G_a$ as an algebraic group is an invertible polynomial fixing zero, and the degree of its polynomial inverse forces degree one. Therefore $u_\alpha(a)n_sB$ corresponds to $[ca:1]$, an isomorphism from $\mathbf A^1$ to the complement of $B$.

The inverse image in $P$ of this affine chart is exactly $Bn_sB$, with its locally closed scheme structure: its points have the unique expression $u_\alpha(a)n_sb$. More precisely, the inverse to the asserted multiplication map is
$$p\longmapsto\bigl(a(\bar p),(u_\alpha(a(\bar p))n_s)^{-1}p\bigr),$$
where $a$ is the regular coordinate of the preceding step. The second component belongs to $B$ by equality in the quotient sheaf; this is the torsor identity, not a test only on field points. Thus both maps are regular scheme morphisms. The other fibre of the two-stratum decomposition is $B$ itself. For every algebraically closed extension $K/F$, every point above $[a:1]$ lies in $B(K)n_sB(K)$ by this formula, and every point above $[1:0]$ lies in $B(K)$. The images in $P/B$ are disjoint. This gives the stated disjoint decomposition of $P(K)$.

source.place: 21.91, pp.453--454; the preceding explicit quotient coordinates

proof.text:
For $t\in T(A)$ use the root conjugation identity and the fact that $n_s$ normalizes $T$:
$$t u_\alpha(a)n_s=u_\alpha(\alpha(t)a)n_s(n_s^{-1}tn_s).$$
The final factor is in $T(A)\subseteq B(A)$, so it disappears on taking right cosets. This proves the asserted left $T$-action $a\mapsto\alpha(t)a$ over every commutative $F$-algebra $A$. No differential of $\alpha$, nor division by the characteristic, occurs.

Since $B\subseteq P$, the coset map $gB\mapsto gP$ is well defined on fppf quotient sheaves and thus gives the morphism $q_\alpha:Q\to H_\alpha$. Take the finite Zariski covering $V_i$ of $H_\alpha$ with sections $s_i:V_i\to G$ from the standard-parabolic lemma. Its torsor identity identifies $G|_{V_i}$ with $V_i\times P$ by $(x,p)\mapsto s_i(x)p$. Dividing by the right action of $B$ gives inverse morphisms
$$V_i\times(P/B)\longleftrightarrow q_\alpha^{-1}(V_i),\quad (x,pB)\mapsto s_i(x)pB,$$
whose inverse is $gB\mapsto(gP,s_i(gP)^{-1}gB)$. The quotient-sheaf meaning makes these formulas valid also when $g$ or $p$ exists only fppf locally. Together with step 4 this proves the required Zariski local triviality with fibre $\mathbf P^1_F$.

source.place: 21.91, pp.453--454; 25.9(a), pp.545--546; associated quotient computed using the displayed local sections

proof.text: The fibre of $q_\alpha$ at the identity coset $o=P$ is $P/B$ scheme-theoretically: after fppf lifting a point to $g\in G$, the equality $gP=P$ is exactly the condition $g\in P$. The point $o:\operatorname{Spec}F\to H_\alpha$ is a closed immersion: it is a section of the separated structure morphism of the proper scheme $H_\alpha$, hence a pullback of its closed diagonal. Closed immersions are preserved by base change, so $Q\times_{H_\alpha}\operatorname{Spec}F\to Q$ is a closed immersion. This identifies the stated fibre as the closed subscheme $P/B\subseteq Q$, with the quotient structure already used above.

source.place: 21.91 and the torsor description; separatedness and pullback of the diagonal

proof.text: Refine the local products of step 8 by the two affine charts of $\mathbf P^1$. Each resulting open subscheme $W\subseteq Q$ is identified with $\mathbf A^1_{V_i}=V_i\times_F\mathbf A^1_F$, and $q_\alpha|_W$ is the projection to $V_i$ followed by the inclusion $V_i\hookrightarrow H_\alpha$. Since $V_i$ is open in $H_\alpha$, the scheme $\mathbf A^1_{V_i}$ is the open subscheme of $\mathbf A^1_{H_\alpha}$ lying over $V_i$, so the same map is the composite $\mathbf A^1_{V_i}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{H_\alpha}\to H_\alpha$ of an open immersion with the projection. The projection is smooth by affine-space smoothness, hence the composite is smooth by the open-immersion composition lemma. These open subschemes $W$ cover $Q$ and smoothness is local on the source, so $q_\alpha$ is smooth.

source.place: Tag 01V5 (smooth morphisms), open immersion followed by a smooth morphism is smooth, smoothness local on the source; affine-space chart

proof.text: For projectivity first identify $Q$ with the projective Borel variety $X=\mathcal B(G)$ supplied by the general-Borel-flag lemma. The point $b_B$ has scheme-theoretic stabilizer $B$, so the homogeneous-orbit lemma identifies its reduced locally closed orbit $O$ with $G/B=Q$. The action is transitive on $X(F)$, so $O$ contains every $F$-point of $X$. Because $X$ is finite type over the algebraically closed field, its closed points are $F$-points and are dense in every closed subset. Thus the closure of $O$ is $X$. A dense locally closed orbit is open. Its closed complement has no closed points, so is empty. An open subset with full underlying space is the whole open subscheme. Since $X$ is smooth over $F$, smooth geometric reducedness makes it reduced, so its reduced orbit structure agrees with that open subscheme. Consequently $Q\simeq X$ and $Q$ is projective over $F$.

source.place: 17.2--17.9, pp.352--354; 7.18, p.142; identification with the projective Borel variety

proof.text: The standard-parabolic lemma makes $H_\alpha$ proper over $F$, hence separated over $F$. Apply the finite-constant projective-graph lemma with $k=F$ and the trivial extension $F/F$, $R=Q$, which embeds in a finite projective space over $F$ by step 11, $S=H_\alpha$ and $c=q_\alpha$. It gives $N\geq0$ and a closed immersion $i:Q\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_F$ such that $(i,q_\alpha):Q\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_F\times_F H_\alpha=\mathbf P^N_{H_\alpha}$ is a closed immersion over $H_\alpha$, and it also gives that $q_\alpha$ is proper, hence of finite type and quasi-compact. Thus $q_\alpha$ is H-projective and quasi-compact, which is projectivity in precisely the convention of the item. All constructions used matrices of determinant one, group-scheme isomorphisms, and the stated characteristic-free structural lemmas. They apply without exception in characteristic two; the sign $-1$ simply equals $1$ there.
